nexa.toolDone: Built in the AWS console, as the brief requires; my partner added a CloudFormation template as an extra.

nexa.svgD: A VPC on AWS with a web tier in a public subnet, an app tier and a data tier in private subnets, security groups between the tiers, and a NAT for outbound OS updates.
nexa.nSgWeb: Security group of the web tier
nexa.nSgApp: Security group of the app tier
nexa.nSgData: Security group of the data tier
nexa.aBlk: Try to reach the database from the internet
nexa.note: private = no way in from the internet
desc: Customers reach the web tier from the internet, through its security group. The web tier is in a public subnet.
The web tier calls the app tier, and the app tier queries the data tier. Both are in private subnets.
A security group sits in front of each tier and controls which tier can talk to which.
A NAT lets the private tiers download OS updates, outbound only. Nothing can reach them from the internet.
facts: VPC 10.20.0.0/16 with three tiers (web, app, data) across two Availability Zones
Public subnets for web, private ones for app and data, one per zone (diagram simplified)
One security group per tier; every resource tagged
NAT: the private tiers only go out for OS updates

ld.h: Logística Directa S.A. · a migration plan to AWS
ld.chip: Course project · module 5160 · pair · presented in class (10-min talk, 16 slides)
ld.case: Case-study company: all costs are projections.
ld.part: My part: co-author of the written plan; in the talk I presented the problem, the context and the conclusions (cost and payback).
ld.svgD: An on-premises data centre linked to AWS in eu-west-1 (Ireland) in a hybrid model; EC2 Auto Scaling from 2 to 10 instances; RDS Multi-AZ with a primary and a standby database; AWS DMS copying the data; the cutover over one weekend.
desc: The on-premises data centre of a case-study company connects to AWS in a hybrid model.
On AWS, in the eu-west-1 region (Ireland), EC2 Auto Scaling runs between 2 and 10 instances.
The database moves to RDS Multi-AZ, with a primary and a standby.
AWS DMS copies about 1.6 TB (full load, then CDC), and the cutover happens over one weekend.
facts: Plan to migrate an on-premises data centre to AWS (case-study company)
EC2 Auto Scaling from 2 to 10 instances · RDS Multi-AZ
AWS DMS (full load + CDC) for ≈1.6 TB · cutover over one weekend

i.updates: Servers outside the VPC that provide the operating-system updates.
i.vpc: The private network that contains all three tiers.
i.web: Web tier, in a public subnet: the part customers reach.
i.app: App tier, in a private subnet: not reachable from the internet.
i.data: Data tier, in a private subnet: not reachable from the internet.
i.nat: Lets the private tiers download OS updates, outbound only.
i.sg: Firewalls that control which tier can talk to which.
i.op: The case-study company's current data centre, the starting point of the plan.
i.hyb: Hybrid model: the on-premises environment and AWS, connected and working together.
i.region: The AWS region chosen in the plan: eu-west-1, in Ireland.
i.asg: Adds or removes EC2 instances with demand: never fewer than 2, never more than 10.
i.stb: RDS Multi-AZ: a standby copy that takes over if the primary fails.
i.dms: Copies the data to AWS: a full load of ≈1.6 TB, then the ongoing changes (CDC).
i.cut: The final switch to AWS, planned over one weekend.

c.req1: → the request reaches the web tier (public subnet)
c.req2: → the web tier calls the app tier (private subnet)
c.req3: → the app tier queries the data tier (private subnet)
c.req4: ← the response returns to the customer
c.upd1: → the app tier goes out through the NAT for OS updates (the data tier does the same)
c.upd2: ✓ outbound only: nothing can come in this way
c.blk: ✕ blocked: the data tier is private (no way in from the internet), and its security group is a second barrier
c.mig2: AWS DMS · CDC: ongoing changes replicated
